LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To ask and answer questions about familiar topics 
(personal information, clothes, colours, weather, etc.).
•	 To understand and talk about dates and numbers.
•	 To talk about things you can see in different places 
in the world and things you can buy or do in a shop.

BEFORE CLASS
Prepare and label your Ss’ material beforehand.
•	 Prepare and label the right number of Story 2 Student 
Books.

Check the teacher’s dashboard to see if the Ss have completed

LESSON PLAN
1.– WARM-UP ROUTINES (13’)
•	 Hello + register + booklets
•	 Moods version 1, TR#4

•	 Calendar

2.– STORY (PP.2-7) (9’) 
Tell the students the first half of the story using the Big 
Book. Please see the section on storytelling in the Warm-Up 
Routines Index.
3.– WORKSHEET: STORY COMPREHENSION (P.3) (9’)
Story Comprehension
3
MATERIALS
•	 Pencils or crayons
In this worksheet, Ss must identify whether the combinations 
of characters and actions are correct or incorrect and tick or 
cross the corresponding box. 
Start by reviewing the worksheet vocabulary with the Ss. 
Simply point to each of the eight boxes and say what the 
character is doing or what the characters are doing, for example: 
“Grandpa is going to the toyshop.”. Have the Ss repeat after you.
Once you have reviewed the language, give out the student 
books saying, “Look! These are your student books for Story 2: 
The Toyshop!”, and have the Ss ask you for the book by saying 
“Can I have my book, please?”
Introduce the activity by saying, “Let’s see if you remember 
where the characters are going in the story!”. Point to the first 
box and say, “Grandpa is going to the toyshop.”; the Ss should 
respond, “No, that’s wrong. Grandpa is going to the doctor’s.” 
Then all the students draw a cross in the box below grandpa 
and the toyshop. 
After you have modelled the task, divide the class into two 
teams. One team will say one phrase and the other should 
respond with the correct statement. Then, switch roles so both 
teams get to practise both structures. You can use a ball to pass 
around each team to indicate whose turn it is to say a phrase.

> Structures (From top to bottom, left to right)
•	 Team 1: “Grandpa is going to the toyshop.”
•	 Team 2: “No, that’s wrong. He is going to the doctor’s.”
•	 Team 1: “Pam and Paul are going to the toyshop.”
•	 Team 2: “Yes, that’s right. They are going to the 
toyshop.”
•	 Team 1: “Mum is going to the hairdresser’s.”
•	 Team 2: “Yes, that’s right. She is going to the 
hairdresser’s.”
•	 Team 1: “Dad is doing the gardening.”
•	 Team 2: “Yes, that’s right. He is doing the gardening.”
> Switch Roles
•	 Team 2: “Dad is going to the newsagent’s.”
•	 Team 1: “No, that’s wrong. He is doing the gardening.”
•	 Team 2: “Mum is going to the sweet shop.”
•	 Team 1: “No, that’s wrong. She is going to the 
hairdresser’s.”
•	 Team 2: “Pam and Paul are playing in the park.”
•	 Team 1: “No, that’s wrong. They are going to the 
toyshop.”
•	 Team 2: “Grandma is going to the doctor’s.”
•	 Team 1: “Yes, that’s right. She is going to the doctor’s.”
NOTE: if your Ss need support, you can show them the pages 
from the story which show what the characters are doing (pp.2-
4). For example, you could open the Big Book to the page where 
Grandpa and Grandma talk about their doctor’s appointment 
and ask, “Are Grandpa and Grandma going to the toyshop?”. 
Ss should look at the Big Book and say, “No, that’s wrong. 
They are going to the doctor’s.”
4.– TOYSHOP SONG, P.12 (TR#12) (2’)
The Toyshop Song
On!
Go!

Have the Ss sing the song while pointing at the worksheet

modelling the task (i.e., showing them where to point based on

5.– ACTIVITY 1: CHARACTER MATCHING (9’)
P.2.1
P.2.1
> Warm-Up
Quickly review the actions that each character is doing by 
putting the Place cards (P.2.1) down on the table. Say, “Grandpa 
and Grandma are going to the doctor’s, Mum is going to the 
hairdresser’s, and Dad is doing the gardening.”
Show the Ss the X cards and ask, “Why can’t Mum take 
Pam and Paul to the toyshop?”, to which they should reply, 
“Because she is going to the hairdresser’s.” Continue in this 
manner until you have gone over all the pairs.
> Main Activity
To introduce the activity, say, “Let’s see if you remember 
what Pam and Paul’s family are doing!”. Put the P.2.1 cards 
in two piles face down: X cards on one side, Place cards on 
the other. The Ss must flip a card from each pile to match the 
character with the correct reason for them to not be able to 
take Pam and Paul to the toyshop.
If they have a match, they should say, “Mum can’t take 
Pam and Paul to the toyshop, because she is going to the 
hairdresser’s. I’ve got a pair!” If they don’t, they should say 
“I’ve got Grandpa and Grandma and doing the gardening; it’s 
not a pair, what a shame!”
> Correct matches and structures
•	 Mum + going to the hairdresser’s: “Mum (she) can’t take 
Pam and Paul to the toyshop because she is going to 
the hairdresser’s.” 
•	 Dad + doing the gardening: “Dad (he) can’t take Pam and 
Paul to the toyshop because he is doing the gardening.”

•	 Grandma and Grandpa + going to the doctor’s: “Grandma 
and Grandpa (they) can’t take Pam and Paul to the 
toyshop because they are going to the doctor’s.”
> Follow-Up
Quickly split the group into two teams. Show team A the X 
card and team B the matching place card. Each team should 
say the part of the structure corresponding to their card. For 
example:
•	 Team A: “Grandpa and Grandma can’t take Pam and 
Paul to the toyshop...”
•	 Team B: “...because they are going to the doctor’s.”

> How to Play
Each S will take a food cutout from a cloth bag and their 
classmates will help them to stick it on the Supermarket sheet 
(P.2.2) by giving them instructions on where to place it.
> Warm-Up
Quickly review the prepositions using your hands: next to, 
between, behind, in front of and opposite. Then review the names 
of the different cutouts found in the cloth bag by asking, “What 
are these?/What is this?” and get the S to reply using a full 
structure, “They are cherries./It is a turkey!”. Continue in this 
manner until you have gone over all the food items.

> Main Activity
Put all the activity cutouts in a cloth bag. Pair up the Ss (S1 and 
S2). Tell the Ss, “Let’s put the food items in the supermarket!”. 
To do the activity, proceed as follows:
•	 S1: Takes a food cutout.
•	 S2: “What have you got?”
•	 S1: “I’ve got lettuce.”
•	 S2: “Where does the lettuce go?”
•	 S1: “The lettuce goes ....” and places the cutout on the 
correct spot using Blu-Tack.
> Follow-Up
To follow up, ask Ss where the different items are. For example, 
“Jane, where does the lettuce go?”, to which Jane will have to 
answer, “The lettuce goes next to the cherries.”
7.– ACTIVITY 8: TAKE A WALK (VERSION 1) (TR#14) (6’)
P.2.3
> How to Play
This version of this activity is played like the musical chairs 
game.
> Warm-Up
Place the A3 Map (P.2.3) in the middle of the table and do a 
little warm-up by saying “If you find the charity shop, point it 
out to me!” and have all your Ss point to the right place on the 
map. Continue in this manner until you have gone over some 
of the shops that are mentioned in the song.
> Main Activity
Introduce the activity by saying, “Let’s take a walk around 
town!”. Leave the map on the table and play the song Take a 
Walk Version 1 (TR#14). The Ss should walk around the table 
singing the song but, when you pause the track after each 
shop, the first S to point to the correct shop on the map should 
sit down so that the rest of their classmates can have a go at 
this activity as well.

If time allows, ask each S, “What can you buy at the...?” 
and the Ss individually, each saying a different item, should 
say, “You can buy  ... at the...”. Challenge them to come up with 
items they haven’t learned in class.

9.– TIME TO GO HOME (TR#20) (2’) 
Sing the Time to Go Home song and have the Ss form a line 
before leaving the class. 
BONUS
ACTIVITY 6: FREEZE!
P.2.5
> Main Activity
The Ss sit on the floor in a circle. Tell them, “Let’s see if 
you remember what you can buy at each shop!”. Place the 
pile of Shop cards (P.2.5) face down in the middle of the circle

and get the Ss to begin passing the ball. Tell them that when 
you say “Freeze!”, they must stop. Whenever you feel like it, 
shout out “FREEZE!” and the S holding the ball must pick up 
a card from the middle of the circle and answer the question, 
“What can you buy at the…?” as quickly as possible. Once Ss 
are used to the game you can make it more dynamic by not 
asking them the question and letting them come up with the 
sentence themselves. For example:
•	 You can buy jumpers at the clothes shop.
•	 You can buy video games at the toy shop.
•	 You can buy muffins at the bakery.
NOTE: you can also play songs from the story to make it 
more dynamic. You can still say “Freeze!” every time you pause 
the song.
> Follow-Up
To follow-up, try to confuse your Ss by saying wrong statements 
about the different shops, for example, “You can buy tomatoes 
at the shoe shop.” to which Ss should answer, “No, you can’t. 
You can buy tomatoes at the greengrocer’s.” 
ACTIVITY 7: DIRECTIONS SONG (TR#13)
> Warm-Up
Review “left”, “right” and “straight ahead” with the Ss. Drill 
the expressions “Turn right!”, “Turn left!” and “Go straight 
ahead!”, asking them to move accordingly.
You can make it more dynamic by eliminating the Ss who 
make a mistake.
> Main Activity
To perform the song, have the Ss stand with their back against 
the wall in a line, side by side. Then the first time they sing the 
song they will simply turn left and right while standing in place 
and then walk straight ahead when the song says to do so. 
The second time you do the activity, they must line up behind 
one another forming a train, holding onto the shoulders of the 
S in front of them. Then, this time, when the song says turn left 
and right, they will actually walk around the room while doing 
so. The song will speed up so make sure the Ss are ready to 
do the actions quickly. 
DIRECTIONS SONG
Turn left, left, left
Turn right, right, right
Walk straight ahead

Straight, straight, straight
That was great! Now line up! Ready? Steady? Go! 
Turn left, left, left
Turn right, right, right
Walk straight ahead
Straight, straight, straight
(repeat) 
Very good! Now let’s go faster!
Turn left, left, left
Turn right, right, right
Walk straight ahead
Straight, straight, straight
(repeat)
